concepts.def: Rostow (1960) five stages: traditional, preconditions, take-off, drive to maturity, high mass consumption.
Frank (1967): development of the West caused underdevelopment of the South; metropolis-satellite chains of exploitation.
Wallerstein (1974): global economy divided into core, semi-periphery and periphery in unequal exchange.
UNDP composite of life expectancy, education and GNI per capita; UK scored 0.929 in 2022, Niger 0.394.
Washington Consensus: free trade, deregulation, privatisation; criticised for widening inequality (Stiglitz 2002).
UN 2015: 17 goals targeting 2030 - poverty, hunger, gender, climate; successor to Millennium Development Goals.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Global Development — a core area of A-Level Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Global Development brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Global Development.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How did Marx define social class?
options: Marx defined class by how much money people earn.
By relationship to the means of production: the bourgeoisie own productive resources; the proletariat sell their labour. Class is a structural relationship, not just income level.
Marx defined class by occupational status like the Registrar General.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between material and cultural deprivation?
options: Material deprivation refers to lack of physical/economic resources (housing, books, food); cultural deprivation refers to lack of skills, values and norms (e.g. parental attitudes to education) that are claimed to support achievement.

sequence.def: Rostow's stage 1: subsistence farming, limited technology
Stage 2: infrastructure, trade and elites emerge
Stage 3: industrialisation and self-sustained growth begin
Stage 5: consumer society, like the modern West
